note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a Const 12(2)(b); A06b Const 12(2)(b); L05 No provision): ordinary naturalisation after 10 years' residence; no renunciation of other citizenships required; a citizen keeps it on taking another. Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given. Citizenship at birth is read from the same dataset's 2024 coding of modes A01a (descent, born in country: Group restriction: only if citizen parent is member of a particular group, race or religion), A01b (descent, born abroad: Group restriction: only if citizen parent is member of a particular group, race or religion), A02a (birth in country: Group restriction: only if parent is member of a particular group, race or religion) and A02b (birth in country to a parent born there: No provision), as its codebook (RSC/GLOBALCIT 2025/01, sections 3.2.1a to 3.2.2b) defines them: by birth in the territory only on the condition the dataset states; by descent from either parent, a child born abroad on the limit the dataset states. The coding also records a restriction to members of a particular group, which the form holds only in the condition's words, which the form doesn't hold. Changes to the law at birth after 1 January 2024 weren't checked for this file. On 2026-11-03 the primary was read: The Uganda Citizenship and Immigration Control Act, Chapter 66 (Laws of Uganda 2000 edition, before the 2009 amendment), Directorate of Citizenship and Immigration Control PDF, ss 12, 14, 16; The Uganda Citizenship Regulations, 2009 (Statutory Instrument), Directorate of Citizenship and Immigration Control PDF, reg. 10. It confirmed loss on taking another citizenship, birth in the territory and descent. It was silent on the years of residence and renunciation, which still rest on the sources above, re-read that day and found the same.

sources.said: Person has legally and voluntarily migrated to Uganda and has been living there for at least 10 years. ... sources.title: The Uganda Citizenship and Immigration Control Act, Chapter 66 (Laws of Uganda 2000 edition, before the 2009 amendment), Directorate of Citizenship and Immigration Control PDF, ss 12, 14, 16
sources.said: 12. Citizenship by birth. The following persons shall be citizens of Uganda by birth— (a) every person born in Uganda one of whose parents or grandparents is or was a member of any of the indigenous communities existing and residing within the borders of Uganda as at the first day of February, 1926, and set out in the Third Schedule to the Constitution; and (b) every person born in or outside Uganda one of whose parents or grandparents was at the time of birth of that person a citizen of Uganda by birth. ... 14. ... (2) ... (b) every person who has legally and voluntarily migrated to and has been living in Uganda for at least twenty years; ... 16. ... (5) The qualifications for naturalisation are that he or she— (a) has resided in Uganda for an aggregate period of twenty years;

sources.title: The Uganda Citizenship Regulations, 2009 (Statutory Instrument), Directorate of Citizenship and Immigration Control PDF, reg. 10
sources.said: 10. Dual Citizenship (1) A citizen who holds the citizenship of any other country in addition to the citizenship of Uganda shall register as a dual citizen in Uganda. (2) The application for registration as a dual citizen under section 19 (D) of the Act shall be in Form AA as set out in the Third Schedule.
